question: Counselor here. A student's SAI is 16,200 but family AGI meets the minimum Pell income test. Any Pell for 2026-27?
must_not_include: is eligible for the minimum Pell
reference_answer: No. For 2026-27, an applicant with an SAI equal to or greater than twice the maximum Pell Grant, $14,790, is ineligible for Pell even if they'd otherwise meet the minimum Pell income test. The only exception is the Special Rule for dependents of certain deceased servicemembers and public safety officers.

sources.title: (APP-25-23) 2026-27 FAFSA Form and Pell Grant Eligibility Updates

question: whats the biggest pell grant check anyone can get this school year (2026-27)?
reference_answer: The 2026-27 maximum Pell Grant is $7,395, and the minimum is $740. Actual awards depend on SAI, cost of attendance and enrollment.

sources.title: (GEN-26-01) 2026-27 Federal Pell Grant Maximum and Minimum Award Amounts

question: My state merit scholarship plus my college's grant add up to more than my full cost of attendance. Is Pell still coming?
reference_answer: Starting in 2026-27, a student can't receive Pell for an award year in which non-federal grants and scholarships equal or exceed the cost of attendance. The school must either reduce the non-federal aid below the cost of attendance or return the Pell and cancel future disbursements. Students who get a maximum Pell under the special rule for children of fallen servicemembers or public safety officers are exempt.

sources.title: Final rule: Accountability in Higher Education and Access through Demand-driven Workforce Pell (Federal Register, May 19, 2026)

question: Is there any federal grant for a 10-week truck driving certificate? Pell used to not cover short stuff.
reference_answer: Starting July 1, 2026, Workforce Pell can cover approved short-term workforce programs that run at least 8 weeks but less than 15 weeks and at least 150 but fewer than 600 clock hours. The specific program must be approved by the state's Governor and the Department, so ask the school.

sources.title: Final rule: Accountability in Higher Education and Access through Demand-Driven Workforce Pell (May 19, 2026)

question: I finished my MBA years ago. Can I get Workforce Pell for a 12-week IT certificate?
must_not_include: yes, you can use workforce pell
reference_answer: No. A student who has already earned a graduate credential, or is enrolled or accepted into a program leading to one, can't receive Pell for an eligible workforce program. Bachelor's degree holders can, if otherwise eligible.

sources.title: Final rule: Accountability in Higher Education and Access through Demand-driven Workforce Pell (Federal Register, May 19, 2026)
2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 7, Ch. 1: Student Eligibility for Pell Grants

question: How many years total can someone collect Pell before it runs out?
reference_answer: Pell has a lifetime limit of 600% Lifetime Eligibility Used, equal to six Scheduled Awards, which is roughly six years or 12 semesters of full-time enrollment. Part-time awards use less of the limit.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 7, Ch. 8: Pell Grant Lifetime Eligibility Used (LEU)
34 CFR Part 690: Federal Pell Grant Program (eCFR)

question: Got full Pell in fall and spring. Can I get more for summer, and do I have to be full time?
reference_answer: Through Year-Round Pell, a student may receive up to 150% of the Scheduled Award in an award year, which can pay for a summer term. The student must be enrolled at least half-time in that payment period, and the school confirms eligibility.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 7, Ch. 5: Summer Terms, Crossover Payment Periods, and Year-Round Pell
34 CFR 690.67: Receiving additional Pell Grant funds in an award year (eCFR)

question: Pell question: if I enroll in 6 credits where full time is 12, what share of my Pell do I get that term?
reference_answer: At a school where 12 credits is full time, 6 credits is 50% enrollment intensity, so the Pell for that term is reduced to match. Part-time students are still eligible, and the aid office does the calculation.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 7, Ch. 3: Pell Grant Enrollment Intensity and Cost of Attendance

question: I took TEACH Grants and now I'm going into nursing instead. What do I owe and does interest start now?
reference_answer: If the teaching service isn't completed, all TEACH Grants convert to Direct Unsubsidized Loans that must be repaid in full, with interest charged from the date of each grant disbursement. A recipient who won't teach can request conversion early to stop further interest from building up.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 9, Ch. 2: TEACH Grant Counseling and the Agreement to Serve or Repay

question: The aid office says they're out of FSEOG money. Isn't that grant guaranteed if I qualify?
reference_answer: No. FSEOG is campus-based: each school gets a limited allocation and awards it until it runs out. Students with the lowest SAIs who also receive Pell have first consideration.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 6, Ch. 6: The Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grant Program
2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 6, Ch. 6: The Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grant Program

question: I dropped out after about 65% of the semester. Do I have to give back some of my Pell?
reference_answer: After the 60% point of the payment period, a student has earned 100% of the federal aid for that period, so withdrawing at about 65% generally means no unearned Pell from the withdrawal calculation. The school runs the calculation and can confirm.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 5, Ch. 1: General Requirements for Withdrawals and the Return of Title IV Funds

question: ok so grants and loans, which one do I actually have to pay back?
reference_answer: Loans must be repaid, usually with interest. Grants and scholarships are gift aid you don't have to earn or pay back, except in specific cases like withdrawing early or an overpayment.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 3, Ch. 3: Packaging Aid
2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 4, Ch. 3: Overawards and Overpayments

question: Can a student whose parent died on active duty still apply for the Iraq and Afghanistan Service Grant by itself?
must_not_include: still available as a separate grant
apply separately for the Iraq and Afghanistan Service Grant
reference_answer: That support now comes through the Pell Grant Special Rule, which lets an eligible student whose parent or guardian died in the line of duty receive the maximum Pell Grant regardless of SAI. Only students with legacy IASG or Children of Fallen Heroes status who keep receiving a disbursement each year stay under the older guidance.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 7, Ch. 1: Student Eligibility for Pell Grants

question: If I file my FAFSA am I guaranteed to get a grant from my state?
must_not_include: you will get a state grant
reference_answer: I can't promise a state grant. Most states use FAFSA information to award their own aid, but each state sets its own rules and deadlines, some very early. Check your state's deadline and ask your financial aid office or state agency what you'd need.

sources.title: 2026-27 FAFSA Form (PDF)
sources.section: Deadlines; How FAFSA information is used

question: Parent working abroad: does my foreign earned income exclusion matter for my son's Pell this year?
reference_answer: Yes. Starting with 2026-27, the foreign earned income exclusion reported on the FAFSA is added to AGI when deciding maximum and minimum Pell eligibility. It isn't added to AGI in the SAI formula, where it is counted as untaxed income instead.
